title: Sensor platform entry
description: Schema for a single sensor platform definition file. The pipeline block is the entire per-sensor spec (tier_structures was retired 2026-07-28; its file-detail knowledge lives in per-stage artifacts and pipeline.optional_extras).

description.description: Short human-readable description of the sensor platform.

tier_structures.description: DEPRECATED (2026-07-28) — per-tier expected/optional folder layouts. Superseded by the pipeline block (per-stage done_when + artifacts); retained for sensors that have not yet been given a pipeline. Remove when the sensor gains one.

folderMap.description: Map of folder glob (relative to the run folder) to list of expected file entries. Use "" for the folder itself.

oneOf.description: Glob pattern for an expected file.

payload.description: Payload this file belongs to (subset of pipeline.payloads); its absence only matters if the payload was intended/captured.

pipeline.description: Ordered processing pipeline for P9 status tracking. Steps are named stages (not 1:1 with tier folders). Sensors without this block are reported as 'no pipeline defined' (never guessed). Readers infer a step done from later steps ONLY when it is marked ephemeral (its evidence is destroyed by a later step); for persistent steps a failed rule is real signal (e.g. raw_cleanup done while qc_report missing = QC was skipped). Optional per-project extras (plot extraction, spectral indices) are deliberately NOT pipeline steps.

payloads.description: Sub-sensor payloads carried by this platform (multi-payload sensors only). Operator-facing names used in issue-YAML intended_payloads/failed_payloads.

deployables.description: Physical field equipment placed per run (e.g. gcps, elm_panels, val_panels). Unlike payloads these are not data streams: if a deployable was not placed (recorded as a deviation / in the issue YAML), rules gated on it via 'requires' become N/A — skipped, never failed. Deployables are assumed placed unless the run records otherwise.

optional_extras.description: Per-project optional products (e.g. Plot_Extraction, SpectralIndices). NOT pipeline stages: absence is never a stall.

name.description: Machine key for the stage (e.g. download, bundle, process, qc_testing, qc_report, raw_cleanup).

ephemeral.description: True if this step's evidence is destroyed by a later step (e.g. download folders deleted by raw_cleanup). Readers may infer an ephemeral step done when any later step is done; never for persistent steps.

done_when.description: One rule, or a list of rules that must ALL hold.

payload_artefacts.description: Optional per-payload artefact glob (relative to the run folder). Keys must be a subset of pipeline.payloads. Only list payloads that produce a distinguishable artefact at this stage — payloads without an entry are not assessed here (e.g. spectral QC exists only for hyperspectral payloads).

artifacts.description: Full expected-file detail for this stage (deep validation, P9 M5). Not used by the cheap done_when probe.

doneRule.description: Composable folder-state rule. Either 'any_of' (alternative sub-rules, ANY passing suffices) or 'folder' plus at least one predicate (all given predicates must hold).

any_of.description: Alternative sub-rules — the rule passes when ANY sub-rule passes (dual-rule transitions, e.g. legacy vs contract QC report filenames). 'requires' / 'primary_only' gates stay on the outer rule; other predicates are ignored when any_of is present.

folder.description: Base folder glob, relative to the run folder (e.g. T0_raw, T1_proc/QC_data).

primary_only.description: Rule applies only to primary captures. For duplicate runs (RunOverview DuplicateRun=True — reprocessings of another run's raw, which lives with the primary run) the rule is N/A — skipped, never failed. Mark the raw-side rules (download, bundle, in-.graw checks, raw_cleanup); product/QC rules still apply to duplicates.

requires.description: Gate for this rule: names drawn from pipeline.payloads and/or pipeline.deployables that must have been intended/deployed for the rule to apply. A string, or a list whose items are ANDed; an inner list of strings is satisfied by ANY member (e.g. ["panels", ["vnir", "swir"]] = panels AND (vnir OR swir)). When the gate is not met (per the run's issue-YAML intended_payloads / deviations), the rule is N/A — skipped, not failed.

contains.description: Glob (relative to folder), or a list of alternative globs (matches are pooled), that must match at least min_count entries. Alternatives cover format transitions, e.g. GeoJSON preferred / shapefile accepted.

max_count.description: Maximum matches for 'contains'. Exceeding it is failed_check (run blocked), never done — e.g. two *.graw bundles or two *.gpro products in one run is an ambiguous/duplicated state needing curation. Requires 'contains'.

min_size.description: Minimum size (e.g. '10 KB') each 'contains' match must reach — guards against truncated/empty marker files (a ~1 KB elm_coefficients.json means the products are garbage).

json_path.description: Dotted path (e.g. 'status.result') into each 'contains' match, which must parse as JSON. Used with json_equals to assert the file's machine-readable verdict — a report that exists but fails its own check is failed_check, never done. Requires 'contains'.

json_equals.description: Value the json_path lookup must equal in EVERY match, or a list of acceptable values (case-insensitive string compare, e.g. 'pass' or ['pass', 'warn']). Missing path or unparseable JSON also fails.

only.description: Folder must contain NOTHING except entries matching these globs (e.g. cleanup done).

extras_beyond.description: Folder must contain at least one entry NOT matching these globs (e.g. raw download present).
